Half-Life was almost cancelled when Valve showed it to Sierra in 1997 — the publisher thought it wasn't fun enough. Valve scrapped 12 months of work and started over.

In Hex Pong, you control the left paddle with Arrow Up / Arrow Down or W / S while the AI controls the right paddle. In Light Trails, use the arrow keys or WASD to steer and trap the AI before either trail hits a wall or occupied cell. In Star Duel variants, rotate, thrust, and fire with Space while the AI dogfights as player 2. In Block Breakers, move the bottom paddle with Left/Right or A/D while the AI covers the top paddle. In Hex Warlords, move the left shield with Up/Down or W/S, hold Space to catch, and release to launch at the AI castle. In Hex Raid variants, fly the left jet with Arrow keys or WASD, fire with Space, and use Shift for mines when the variant allows them. In Hex Outlaw, dodge visible bullets, line up your shot, and fire with Space or Shift. In Hex Tennis, move across your half, serve with Space or Shift, and let the AI cover the far court. In Hex Invaders, move with Left/Right or A/D, fire with Space, and let the AI clear the other cannon lane. In Hex Enduro, change lanes with Left/Right or A/D, accelerate and brake with Up/Down or W/S, and trigger turbo with Space or Shift. In Hex Skiing, steer with Left/Right or A/D, clear slalom gates, dodge obstacles, and outrun the avalanche when the variant has one. In Hex Frost, move with Arrow keys or WASD, jump between ice rows with Up/Down or W/S, build the igloo, and avoid arctic enemies. In Hex Hockey, skate with Arrow keys or WASD, shoot or tackle with Space or Shift, and challenge the AI from the far side.
In Pixel Tanks, rotate with Left/Right or A/D, drive forward with Up or W, and fire with Space or Shift while the AI navigates the maze as player 2.
In Retro Games solo mode, you control the bottom paddle while the AI controls the top paddle.
In Retro Games solo mode, you control the left boxer while the AI controls the right boxer. Difficulty changes how tightly the AI tracks range, dodges, and times punches.
In Retro Games solo mode, you control the left castle shield while the AI controls the right castle shield.
In Retro Games solo mode, you control the left tank while the AI controls the right tank. Difficulty changes how quickly the AI tracks corridors, dodges missiles, and takes shots.
It is also available in Retro Games solo mode against an AI tank.
